title: Tesla Stock (TSLA) Falls 1.8% to $390.22 (Nov 13)
summary: Tesla (TSLA) fell 1.82% to $390.22 on Nov 13, 2026 as tech stocks slid; Cybercab pre-orders for personal use opened after the close.
body_markdown:
## Why Tesla Stock Fell


None of the sources reviewed named a Tesla-specific cause for Friday's decline, which came on a weak day for technology shares. According to[Investopedia](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-today-futures-tick-133734502.html) , tech stocks fell as the market dealt with the[fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepping down](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/nvidia-without-huang-ppi-tonight/) , chip stocks were broadly under pressure, and rising Treasury yields reflected concerns that the Federal Reserve will raise rates again next month. Investopedia listed Tesla among the mega-cap decliners, down about 2%.


The session followed the[merger reports that lifted Tesla on Thursday](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/tesla-tsla-stock-news-november-13-2026/) . As reported by[Barchart](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/tesla-spacex-merger-could-create-134206442.html) , reports suggest Tesla and SpaceX are advancing merger talks, with a deal possibly announced as early as next month, and Elon Musk confirmed on SpaceX's third-quarter call in October that both boards formed special committees of independent directors. The talks remain reported, with no merger agreement described.


Tesla's own news came after the session. The company announced on X on Friday evening that select customers can pre-order the Cybercab for personal use at $29,990, plus $299 per month to operate it, according to[TechCrunch](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/tesla-opens-cybercab-pre-orders-200444578.html) .


Deliveries are estimated for December 2026, the vehicle will run only inside geofenced areas, and Musk said the monthly fee is "too high." Because the post came after the close, it did not drive Friday's trading.


## TSLA Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- The Cybercab, previously used only in Tesla's robotaxi fleet, is now offered to select buyers, and Tesla lists installed annual capacity of more than 125,000 vehicles, according to[Fox Business](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/tesla-makes-major-cybercab-announcement-014928775.html) .
- Musk said the Cybercab will be available nationwide as Tesla receives regulatory approval, per TechCrunch.
- Both companies' boards have formed special committees of independent directors to study a merger, according to Barchart, keeping a SpaceX combination under formal review.


### Risks


- The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an audit in September into whether Tesla properly self-certified the Cybercab's compliance with federal safety standards; Tesla has told the agency it believes the vehicle meets them, according to Fox Business.
- The Cybercab works only inside geofenced areas, and Musk himself called the $299 monthly fee "too high," per TechCrunch.
- Barchart notes that Tesla's vehicle volumes have declined for two consecutive years, while the SpaceX merger remains at the reported-talks stage.
